title: Talk with people, not at them

unit.title: Talk with people, not at them
unit.needIt: People remember how a conversation felt, not what was said. The ones who let others speak are the ones people want around.
unit.why: Imagine a person who talks for an hour without stopping. Everyone else feels like a statue, just waiting for a turn that never comes. Conversation is a game of catch, not a solo performance.
unit.outcome: Practice pausing before you speak to ensure your words are helpful to the listener.
unit.reachesYou: You see this when a friend dominates a dinner chat or a coworker talks over you at lunch. It happens every time you try to connect with someone new.
unit.do: Next time you are talking to someone, stop after two sentences and ask them a question about their day.

quiz.q: What is the main problem with a 'voluble talker'?
choices: They speak too quietly.
They use too many big words.
They do not give others a chance to speak.
They speak about too many different topics.
quiz.why: The text says the chatterer rides through hours without giving others a chance to speak.
quiz.quote: The voluble talker, or chatterer, rides his own hobby straight through the hours without giving anyone else, who might also .like to say something, a chance to do other than exhaustedly await the turn that never comes.

quiz.q: What is the 'simple rule' to avoid being a bore?
choices: Speak more often.
Stop and think.
Speak only about yourself.
Speak very loudly.
quiz.why: The text identifies stopping and thinking as the primary way to avoid being a pest.
quiz.quote: There is a simple rule, by which if one is a voluble chatterer (to be a good talker necessitates a good mind) one can at least refrain from being a pest or a bore.

quiz.q: Why does the text mention a mother describing a baby's tricks to a bachelor?
choices: To show how oversharing can bore others.
To show how funny babies are.
To explain how to train a baby.
To show how to be a good mother.
quiz.why: The text uses this to show that even friends might not want to hear every tiny detail.
quiz.quote: She would know very well, alas! that not even a very dear friend would really care for more than a hots Hoeuvre of the subject, at the board of general conversation.

quiz.q: What should you do if you find yourself in a disagreement?
choices: Switch to a different subject.
Argue until you win.
Tell the person they are wrong.
Stop talking entirely.
quiz.why: The text says a tactful person switches to a pleasanter channel of conversation.
quiz.quote: If he finds another's opinion utterly opposed to his own, he switches to another subject for a pleasanter channel of conversation.

quiz.q: What is a common mistake people make when asking someone to repeat themselves?
choices: They do it out of habit and inattention.
They do it because they are deaf.
They do it to be rude.
They do it because they are bored.
quiz.why: The text notes that many people say 'What?' due to careless inattention.
quiz.quote: But countless persons with perfectly good hearing say "What?" from force of habit and careless inattention.

quiz.q: What is the 'first, last and only rule' of conversation?
choices: Be funny.
Stop and think.
Listen well.
Speak clearly.
quiz.why: The text explicitly states that stopping and thinking is the only rule.
quiz.quote: Above all, stop and think what you are saying I This is really the first, last and only rule.

partials: Conversation should be equal give and take.
Chatterers do not give others a chance to speak.
Most mistakes happen because people do not think.
You should try to say things agreeable to others.
Stopping and thinking prevents you from being a bore.
crystal.key: Good conversation requires you to stop and think before you speak to ensure a balanced exchange.

decoys.text: The goal is to be the most interesting person in the room.
decoys.why: The text says the goal is to be agreeable and give others a chance to speak, not just to be interesting.

decoys.text: It is okay to repeat stories if they are very funny.
decoys.why: The text says nothing interests when it is told a second time.

crystal.aha: By stopping to think, you move from being a 'take' (a pest) to a 'give' (a good conversationalist).

beats.say: Throw it back, and the game goes on.
Keep it, and there is no game.
Stop and think before you speak, and give the other a turn.

line.label: Conversation is equal give and take.
